assessments.reasoning: Borland’s guide describes units as the usual way to divide program source into modules. It places an optional uses clause between the program heading and the block. Both particulars come from the program-organization passage in the retained guide.

challenge.method: Would a program without a uses clause, or one without the usual division into units, defeat the claim?
challenge.results: Both cases fit the guide’s qualifiers. The evidence establishes the organization described for Borland Object Pascal and supplies no rule for other Pascal dialects.

limitations: This guide itself qualifies the usual program organization. It establishes no universal rule for Apple Object Pascal or all Pascal dialects.
This is the organization described for the Borland variety in the cited guide. Other Object Pascal traditions require their own sources.
